Area.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/1] In all three cases clinical depression was identified, and a contributing element to suicidality, as traced out by the data, was perfectionism. [/page/1/Text/2] The article begins by outlining and comparing definitions of perfectionism and how it has been described in the suicide literature. We then outline a rationale for suggesting why some of the higher education student population may be particularly vulnerable to suicidal ideation and behavior. While perfectionism is unlikely to be the defining feature of an individual who takes their own life, these data about its possible importance are consistent with other psychological theories and research which draw attention to the destructive elements of the relationship between perfectionism and suicide. This article seeks to shed light upon the nature of this relationship and the influence perfectionism may have as a contributory factor to suicide.
